rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however labeled, of more than one month's rent on top of first month's rent. Small natural-person landlords may charge up to two months (see separate rule), and an advance payment of six or more months' rent is allowed on leases of six months or longer.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling; applies to security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords meeting Civ. Code 1950.5(c)(5) (natural person or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total) may charge up to two months, except to service members; advance payment of at least six months' rent on a lease of six months or longer; agreed fees for tenant-requested alterations.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether the landlord qualifies as a small natural-person landlord under (c)(5), which depends on the owner's whole rental portfolio; whether the tenant is a service member; when the security was collected (before July 1, 2024 is exempt).

rules.penalty: Bad-faith retention may lead to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages (Civ. Code 1950.5(m)).
rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is inferred from (c)(6), which exempts security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

rules.title: Small landlord exception: deposit up to two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord that is a natural person (or an LLC whose members are all natural persons) and that owns no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may collect security of up to two months' rent. This exception does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member, and such a landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of the lower cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlord is a natural person (including family trust settlors and beneficiaries) or an LLC with all natural-person members, and owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four rental units in total.
rules.exemptions: Not available when the prospective tenant is a service member; in that case the one-month cap applies.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner must be a natural person, family trust, or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total across the portfolio; tenant must not be a service member.

rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad-faith violations (Civ. Code 1950.5(m)).

rules.title: Service member higher security: written explanation and return within six months
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher-than-standard security based on credit history, credit score, housing history or a similar factor, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and the reason by lease signing. The extra amount must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenant is a service member (as defined in Mil. & Vet. Code 400) renting residential property they will live in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The tenant is a service member, and a higher-than-standard security is charged because of credit or housing history.

rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad-faith violations (Civ. Code 1950.5(m)).
rules.quoted_span: (4) On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.

rules.title: Return of deposit with itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must give an itemized statement of deductions and return the rest of the deposit. Receipts or invoices and photos must accompany the statement unless deductions total $125 or less or the tenant validly waived them. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and cleaning back to the move-in condition.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days; documentation required if deductions exceed $125
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies where security was collected.
rules.exemptions: Receipt and invoice documentation is not required if deductions total $125 or less or the tenant signed a timely waiver, unless the tenant requests documentation within 14 days.
rules.penalty: A landlord who fails to comply in bad faith forfeits any claim to the security; bad-faith retention exposes the landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the security plus actual damages.

rules.title: Required move-in and move-out photographs
rules.requirement: The landlord must photograph the unit after the tenant returns possession, both before and after any repairs or cleaning to be deducted (from April 1, 2025). For tenancies starting on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit at move-in. Photos must accompany any deductions for repairs or cleaning.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies with security deposits.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The move-in photo requirement applies only to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad-faith violations (Civ. Code 1950.5(m)).
rules.quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.conflict_note: The move-out photo requirement took effect April 1, 2025; the move-in photo requirement applies to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.title: No nonrefundable security
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not describe any security deposit or fee as nonrefundable.
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad-faith retention (Civ. Code 1950.5(m)).
rules.quoted_span: (n) A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Electronic return of deposit when paid electronically
rules.requirement: If the landlord received the security or rent electronically, the remaining deposit must be returned electronically to a tenant-designated account unless the parties agree in writing to another method. The landlord must notify the tenant of this right near the end of the tenancy. Where several adult tenants share a unit, the refund goes by a check payable to all of them unless they all agree in writing otherwise.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in which the landlord (or the successor in interest) received the security or rent payments electronically.
rules.exemptions: A prior written agreement designating another return method; terminations under Code Civ. Proc. 1161(2)-(4) (exempt from the notice requirement).
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad-faith violations (Civ. Code 1950.5(m)).
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(h)(1)(A)(ii), as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414)
